ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a circuit composed of 3 cascaded JK flip-flops, and all three flip-flops are drawn with clock input symbols triggered on the falling edge. The JK inputs of each stage are connected into the effective toggle state, namely J=K=1. The 1st flip-flop is triggered by an external CP pulse, and its output Q1 is connected to the clock terminal of the 2nd flip-flop; the output Q2 of the 2nd flip-flop is connected to the clock terminal of the 3rd flip-flop. Asynchronous set/reset terminals are also drawn for each stage, but they do not have a changing effect in the state transition of this problem. Reasoning: The current state is Q3Q2Q1=011, so Q1=1, Q2=1, Q3=0. When J=K=1, a JK flip-flop toggles when it encounters an effective falling edge. The falling edge of the external CP first causes the 1st flip-flop to toggle, and Q1 changes from 1 to 0. Since the 1→0 of Q1 is a falling edge, it serves as the effective clock edge of the 2nd flip-flop, causing Q2 to change from 1 to 0. Since the 1→0 of Q2 is again a falling edge, it serves as the effective clock edge of the 3rd flip-flop, causing Q3 to change from 0 to 1. Therefore the next state is Q3Q2Q1=100.
